articles.title: Ironclad runways: U.S. and Japan reinforce ExR-ADR capabilities during KS27
articles.summary: IRUMA AIR BASE, Japan - U.S., Japan, and Canadian Armed Forces collaborated in expeditionary rapid airfield damage repair (ExR-ADR) training during Exercise Keen Sword 27 at a Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) installation at Iruma Air Base, Japan, Oct. 22-26.

articles.title: U.S. Naval Hospital Okinawa strengthens bilateral medical readiness during Keen Sword 27
articles.summary: CAMP FOSTER, Okinawa, Japan — U.S. Naval Hospital Okinawa personnel trained alongside Japan Self-Defense Forces and joint medical partners during Keen Sword 27, a bilateral exercise that tested the hospital’s ability to receive, triage and treat large numbers of simulated casualties Oct. 26-27.

articles.title: NORAD fighter aircraft execute homeland defense mission from austere Eareckson Air Station
articles.summary: U.S. Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcons maintained air defense alert at Eareckson Air Station, Alaska, during an Oct. 18–26 deployment before launching a homeland defense mission on Oct. 25, integrating aircraft from two other Alaskan bases and one Canadian base.

articles.title: CSAF, CMSAF observe Team Osan mission readiness in action
articles.summary: U.S. Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ken Wilsbach and Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David Wolfe visited Osan Air Base, Republic of Korea, Oct. 22, 2026, gaining firsthand insight into how Team Osan integrates operations, maintenance and support capabilities to sustain readiness on the Korean Peninsula.

articles.title: Army HF Gateway teams demonstrate communications readiness during Noble Skywave
articles.summary: U.S. Army Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM), the 78th Signal Battalion and the 30th Signal Battalion participated in Noble Skywave, a Canadian-hosted high-frequency (HF) communications exercise, last week, testing the skills and adaptability of Army signal professionals operating across a range of communications conditions.

articles.title: Guardsman scores 498 on AFT, outscores team of college athletes
articles.summary: Idaho Army National Guard Chief Warrant Officer 3 Emily Wood faced off against five Boise State University student-athletes in a friendly competition earlier this month, scoring 498 points on the Army Fitness Test to edge the Broncos’ combined score of 496.

articles.title: Hasty US exit from Europe could drive allies away from American arms, RAND says
articles.summary: A rapid, uncoordinated U.S. military drawdown from Europe could push key NATO allies further away from American weapons, a RAND study found.

articles.title: Jaelen Johnston reflects on performance at Friday on the Frontier
articles.summary: As the sun set on the flight line, Jaelen Johnston, local country music artist, performed a free concert for Airmen and their families during Friday on the Frontier, Oct. 23. Johnston is no stranger to McConnell. He was born in Derby and also worked in construction for the Air National Guard 184th Wing before beginning his music career.

articles.title: Signal staff turns up the heat with chili cook-off
articles.summary: The U.S. Army Signal School hosted its 5th Annual Chili Cook-Off, building on camaraderie and friendly competition.

articles.title: Army Assistant Secretary Andersen calls on private capital to rebuild 'Arsenal of Democracy'
articles.summary: The U.S. Army is overhauling its Cold War-era funding framework to partner directly with private capital markets, Assistant Secretary of the Army for Financial Management & Comptroller Marc Andersen shared with an audience of founders, startups, subject-matter experts, vice chairs, private equity, defense primes, military leaders, policymakers…

articles.title: Long Deployments to Be Navy Standard For Next Couple Years, MCPON, CNO Say
articles.summary: It will take a couple years before deployment lengths shift from the extended 10-11 months back to the normal seven, the Navy’s top enlisted sailor said Wednesday. As sailors deploy with carrier strike groups, they are being told to expect a deployment that is between 10-11 months, MCPON John Perryman said while speaking at the Navy Memorial.

articles.title: BS27-1: Defending the base at every level
articles.summary: KADENA AIR BASE, Japan — U.S. Air Force Airmen assigned to the 18th Wing were armed with M-4 carbine rifles and tasked to man defensive firing positions outside their work centers during Exercise Beverly Sword 27-1 at Kadena Air Base, Japan, Oct. 28, 2026.

articles.title: U.S., Partner Nations to Hold Annual Malabar Naval Exercise Near Japan
articles.summary: The United States, Australia, India and Japan will carry out this year’s iteration of the annual Malabar naval exercise in the waters near Japan next week. Malabar 2026 will take place south of the Kanto region on the main island of Honshu from Nov. 5-12, according to a Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force news release published on Tuesday.

articles.title: From waterways to runways, Tulsa District delivers in fiscal year 2026
articles.summary: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Tulsa District, provided community support across multiple missions for fiscal year 2026. This article highlights a few of the projects for the year.

articles.title: New tactical comms system for US ground troops aims to break network silos
articles.summary: "We've spent the past 50 years building siloed networks, siloed applications and siloed environments to collaborate internally with our own data. We can no longer do that," a Pentagon official said.

articles.title: Record deployment for destroyer USS Spruance casts doubt over US Navy maintenance
articles.summary: The Arleigh-Burke class destroyer USS Spruance has set a post-World War II record for a U.S. Navy destroyer deployment and is raising questions about the maintenance work that could follow its eventual return.

articles.title: Pentagon investigates series of commissary freezer failures as possible cyberattack
articles.summary: Refrigeration failures spoiled food at military commissaries across the country. Investigators are examining whether hackers were responsible. The post Pentagon investigates series of commissary freezer failures as possible cyberattack appeared first on Task & Purpose .

articles.title: Senior US general fired, accused of leaking classified information
articles.summary: U.S. Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, a senior military planner on the Pentagon's Joint Staff, was fired over accusations he leaked classified information to the public.

articles.title: Army Reserve’s 1st Brigade, 78th Training Division welcomes new commander
articles.summary: JOINT BASE MCGUIRE-DIX-LAKEHURST, N.J. – The U.S. Army Reserve’s 1st Brigade, 78th Training Division, welcomed its new commander during a traditional change-of-command ceremony Oct. 24 here on Sharp Field.

articles.title: Naval Health Clinic New England Recognized for Support to DoD Global Respiratory Surveillance Program
articles.summary: Naval Health Clinic New England (NHCNE) was formally recognized for its significant contributions to the Department of Defense Global Respiratory Surveillance Program (DoDGRSP) during the 2025–26 respiratory season.
